external_assumptions: Elixir bootstrap compiler and standard library
OTP 29 compiler, ERTS, code loader and crypto provider
Python 3 interpreter and standard library for helpers and source inventory
native drivers/NIFs and approved host executables
operating system, filesystem, process groups, clocks and entropy source
Unicode source tables and local table/vector generators
reviewed build inputs, CI host and explicit trust-root/key provisioning

checks: exact sidecar rebuild and byte comparison
minimum component/catalog/lock replay
altered generated-data inventory refusal
independent clean full-package archive comparison under changed ambient environment
rehashed substituted archive rejected by full rebuild; interrupted staging preserves published bytes
publisher-signed immutable registry artifact identity and exact mirror-byte verification
snapshot-bound lock replay distinguishes yanked history from terminal compromise
residual_trust: canonical serializers and hashes
source compilation, tools and build host can be compromised together
exact reproducibility depends on declared compiler/toolchain and trusted host; atomic publication is not power-loss durability
registry identity depends on provisioned root authority, honest observation time and key custody

checks: canonical schema-directed framing rejects malformed, oversized, unknown and foreign payloads
mutual TLS and the application handshake bind certificate, node, service, package and protocol identity
bounded admission distinguishes not-enqueued work from delivery-unknown in-flight work
message identifiers suppress exact duplicates and reject conflicting duplicates without claiming processing
protocol-version skew is refused before application messages are exchanged
residual_trust: the host TLS and cryptographic implementations correctly authenticate configured certificate chains
operators protect private keys, configure peer fingerprints and revoke compromised identities
partitions after transmission can leave delivery uncertain and application processing unobserved
transport availability, address resolution and operating-system failure remain deployment concerns

checks: compiled/reference conformance
wrong generated result accepted by raw OTP but rejected by exact source-bound artifact comparison
residual_trust: backend correctness and OTP compiler remain trusted
same defective lowering in build and rebuild is not independently checked

checks: governance-erasure fixtures
debug sidecar origin and mutation tests
sealed secret transformations and recipient results retain revocation lineage
sentinel diagnostics, traces, status, crash and artifact refusal tests
residual_trust: lowering and sidecar construction preserve erasure
debugging hosts and exported artifacts are outside a secrecy theorem
secret protection relies on OTP sensitivity, redacted status, approved recipients and trusted host; no secure erasure or hostile-host secrecy

checks: whole-carrier codec refusal
forged authority and expired-handle refusal
native package and platform admission
artifact-derived transitive obligation closure
owner-qualified scoped admission, attenuation and revocation
native registry provenance binds platform, toolchain, content and unsafe obligations
residual_trust: native code can crash or corrupt the VM
external processes and approved executables remain trusted code
OS isolation is not supplied by static typing
host closure disclosure is asserted; already admitted work is not rolled back by revocation

checks: valid/invalid Ed25519 signatures
threshold/revocation/lifecycle tests
signed false content still needs semantic evidence
dual-authority registry root rotation and threshold-signed snapshot fixtures
registry rollback, equivocation, forged publisher and compromise-terminal refusal
residual_trust: configured trust roots and key custody
OTP crypto and its native provider
signatures authenticate bytes, not program correctness

checks: capability non-escape
affine resumption checks
owned cancellation/revocation/cleanup tests
residual_trust: ERTS scheduling and process semantics
host failures can prevent OS cleanup; no rollback or fairness theorem

checks: exact source path and call inventory
new raw compiler/foreign dispatch mutation refusal
guard-only mutation explicitly outside syntax gate
residual_trust: scanner, parsers, baseline review and CI host
syntactic fingerprints are not a semantic security proof or complete information-flow analysis

checks: checked local sends validate and snapshot immutable data before Unit-returning send
invalid payloads are refused before bounded queue admission or capacity accounting
per-sender order survives several producers while cross-sender interleaving remains unspecified
native send-only handles retain live scope and mailbox-codec checks
remote outcomes retain authenticated distribution uncertainty without implicit retry
residual_trust: BEAM immutable storage may be copied or shared because physical identity is not observable
raw local send retains deployment-sized mailbox behavior and no liveness acknowledgement
trusted foreign code can retain physical objects after checked conversion
remote partitions can leave transmitted work delivery-unknown

checks: bounded condition facts and derived evidence checks
ordinary library law suites
forged core evidence refusal
residual_trust: no general executable theorem kernel for every prose proof
promised/tested/derived law levels remain distinct
shared implementations can correlate compiler and oracle faults

checks: bounded trace-set exploration
compiled/reference comparison and counterexample fixtures
residual_trust: models share type/value/codec helpers with implementation
agreement cannot detect every common-mode defect

checks: exact per-unit and aggregate compiler budgets with stable diagnostics
pre-publication aggregate artifact budgeting and transactional package output
explicit message-count and encoded-byte admission with reject/terminate overload outcomes
owner cancellation discards queued work and leaves no silent-loss success
residual_trust: ERTS external_size is deterministic accounting rather than resident-memory measurement
raw local send remains unbounded; callers must select the checked capacity queue
OS/VM fatal exhaustion and scheduler failure remain outside recoverable language behavior

checks: scheduler profile rejects deterministic, fairness and reduction-count claims
foreign and native work receives an exact preemptible or scheduled-blocking class
unclassified and unsafe-unbounded work is refused by the supported profile
scheduled blocking admission has explicit finite worker capacity
bounded explorer retains nondeterministic schedules and reports exhausted evidence bounds
residual_trust: ERTS selects runnable processes, reduction accounting and preemption points
deployment priorities can affect opportunity and latency without changing message order
host code declared cooperative can violate its declaration
no universal fairness, starvation-freedom or timing guarantee is made

checks: retained source/typing/scope conformance
corrupted JSON and kernel core refusal
residual_trust: frontends preserve intended source
shared Type/Data/Row/Coverage helpers can have correlated defects

checks: independent rational/Unicode vectors
collection/outcome/foundation laws
actual selected-library applications
residual_trust: generators, Unicode primary data and host byte/numeric primitives
finite test corpora are not universal proofs
